questions.stem: What is an element?
options: A substance made of only one type of atom
A substance made of two or more atoms chemically joined
A mixture that cannot be separated
questions.explanation: Elements contain one kind of atom only. Two or more kinds chemically joined make a compound.

questions.stem: What is a compound?
options: Two or more elements mixed together
A substance made of one type of atom
Two or more different elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio
questions.explanation: Compounds involve chemical bonding and a fixed ratio. Mixing without bonding gives a mixture.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
questions.explanation: Symbols are one or two letters, with only the first capitalised. Oxygen is O.
questions.teaching:
Chemical symbols follow a strict system, and knowing it removes most of the guesswork.

Each symbol is one or two letters. The first is always a capital and the second, if there is one, is always lower case — which is why CO and Co mean completely different things, one a compound of two elements and the other a single element. Most symbols come from the English name, but a stubborn group of long-known metals take theirs from Latin instead: iron from ferrum, sodium from natrium, potassium from kalium, lead from plumbum, gold from aurum, silver from argentum, copper from cuprum, tin from stannum. Those are the ones worth memorising, because they cannot be worked out.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.explanation: Sodium's symbol comes from its Latin name natrium. S alone is sulfur.

Those are the ones worth memorising, because they cannot be worked out.

questions.stem: What does the formula H2O tell you?
options: Hydrogen and oxygen are mixed but not joined
Each molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom
questions.explanation: The subscript gives the number of atoms of the element before it. No number means one.

questions.stem: How many atoms in total are in one molecule of CO2?
questions.explanation: One carbon plus two oxygens is three atoms.

questions.stem: Which of these is an element?
questions.explanation: Copper is one type of atom. Water and salt are compounds; air is a mixture.
questions.teaching:
Matter is classified by what it is made of, and there are three categories worth separating.

An element contains only one kind of atom and cannot be broken down chemically into anything simpler — these are the entries on the periodic table. A compound has two or more kinds of atom chemically bonded in fixed proportions, so it has properties quite unlike its ingredients. A mixture has substances physically together but not bonded, in any proportion, and can be separated by physical means. Water is a compound; air is a mixture; anything with a single square on the periodic table is the first category.

questions.stem: Which of these is a compound?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide joins two elements chemically. Steel is a mixture (an alloy).

questions.stem: What is an atom?
options: The smallest particle of an element
The same thing as a molecule
questions.explanation: Atoms are the basic units of elements. A molecule is two or more atoms joined.

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign that a chemical change has happened?
options: The substance is cut into pieces
A new substance forms with different properties
questions.explanation: Chemical change makes new substances. Shape change, dissolving and cutting are physical.

questions.stem: Which of these is a physical change?
questions.explanation: Melting changes state but not the substance. The other three make new substances.

questions.stem: Which observation suggests a chemical reaction is occurring?
options: Bubbles of a new gas forming without boiling
A solid being ground into powder
questions.explanation: Gas produced without boiling points to a reaction. The others are all physical.

questions.stem: What is a precipitate?
options: A gas given off in a reaction
The heat released by a reaction
An insoluble solid formed when two solutions react
questions.explanation: A precipitate appears as a cloudiness or solid when solutions are mixed — a classic sign of chemical change.

questions.stem: What are the reactants in a chemical reaction?
options: The substances present in the greatest quantity
The substances left over once the reaction stops
questions.explanation: Reactants go in, products come out.

questions.stem: In the periodic table, what does each box represent?
questions.explanation: The periodic table organises the elements, one box each.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
questions.explanation: Iron's symbol comes from the Latin ferrum. Ir is iridium and I is iodine.

Those are the ones worth memorising, because they cannot be worked out.

questions.stem: Which of these is a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Rust is a new substance with new properties. The others are physical.

questions.stem: What does a chemical formula show?
options: Which elements are present and how many atoms of each
questions.explanation: Formulas give composition, not physical properties.

questions.stem: Is a physical change usually easy to reverse?
options: Yes, because no new substance is made
questions.explanation: Melted ice can be refrozen. Chemical changes are generally much harder to reverse.

questions.stem: What is a molecule?
options: Two or more atoms chemically joined together
questions.explanation: Molecules can be of one element (O2) or of a compound (H2O).

questions.stem: How does a mixture of iron and sulfur differ from the compound iron sulfide?
options: The mixture can be separated with a magnet; the compound cannot
The mixture has a fixed ratio and the compound does not
questions.explanation: In the mixture the iron keeps its magnetic property. Once they react, the new compound has entirely different properties.

questions.stem: How many atoms of each element are in Ca(OH)2?
options: Two calcium, two oxygen, two hydrogen
One calcium, two oxygen, two hydrogen
One calcium, one oxygen, two hydrogen
One calcium, two oxygen, one hydrogen
questions.explanation: The subscript outside the bracket multiplies everything inside, so OH is doubled.

questions.stem: A candle burns and the wax also melts. Which changes are these?
options: Burning is chemical; melting is physical
Burning is physical; melting is chemical
questions.explanation: This is a useful example because both happen at once: melting changes state, burning makes new substances.

questions.stem: Why is a temperature rise alone not proof of a chemical reaction?
options: A temperature rise always means bonds have been broken
Physical processes such as dissolving can also change temperature
Only reactions that release heat count as chemical changes
questions.explanation: Dissolving some salts warms or cools a solution without any reaction. Several signs together are more convincing than one.

questions.stem: Two clear solutions are mixed and turn cloudy white. What has most likely happened?
options: An insoluble precipitate has formed in a chemical reaction
The solutions have simply diluted each other
questions.explanation: Formation of a solid from two clear solutions is a reaction, not a physical mixing.

questions.stem: Why do the symbols Na and Fe not match their English names?
options: They come from the Latin names natrium and ferrum
They are abbreviations of the discoverers' names
They refer to the elements' colours
questions.explanation: Several long-known elements kept symbols from their Latin names, which is why they look mismatched.

questions.stem: Which statement about a compound is correct?
options: Its properties are the average of its elements
It keeps the properties of each element
It can be separated by filtering
Its properties are usually very different from those of its elements
questions.explanation: Sodium is a reactive metal and chlorine a toxic gas, but sodium chloride is table salt. Chemical joining changes properties completely.

questions.stem: A student writes the symbol for cobalt as CO. What is wrong?
options: CO is carbon monoxide; cobalt is Co with a lower-case second letter
CO and Co can be used interchangeably in formulas
questions.explanation: Capitalisation matters: only the first letter of a symbol is capitalised, so CO and Co mean entirely different things.

questions.stem: Which pair correctly matches a change with its type?
questions.explanation: Souring produces new substances. Boiling, dissolving and bending are all physical.

questions.stem: Why is mass conserved in a chemical reaction?
options: New atoms are created to balance the loss
The same atoms are present before and after, just rearranged
Atoms are destroyed and replaced equally
Mass is only conserved in physical changes
questions.explanation: Reactions rearrange atoms; they do not create or destroy them, so total mass is unchanged.

questions.stem: A sealed flask of reacting chemicals shows no mass change, but an open one loses mass. Why?
options: A gas produced escapes from the open flask
Mass is destroyed in open containers
questions.explanation: The gas is still matter. Sealing the system keeps it inside, which is how conservation of mass is demonstrated.

questions.stem: Which classification is correct for stainless steel?
options: An element, because it is a metal
A mixture, because the proportions of its metals can be varied
A compound, because it has a fixed formula
questions.explanation: Alloys are mixtures because their proportions can be varied, which a compound cannot do. Metal atoms in an alloy are still held by metallic bonding — it is the variable composition, not an absence of bonding, that makes it a mixture.

questions.stem: Why can a compound not be separated by filtration, distillation or a magnet?
options: Compounds have no separate elements in them
Compounds have particles that are too small
Those methods exploit physical differences, and a compound's elements are chemically bonded
questions.explanation: Only a chemical reaction can break the bonds. Physical separation works on mixtures only.

questions.stem: Magnesium is burned in air and the product weighs more than the original metal. Explain.
options: Oxygen from the air has combined with the magnesium
Mass has been created in the reaction
The magnesium absorbed heat, which has mass
questions.explanation: The product is magnesium oxide, and the extra mass is the oxygen that joined. Nothing is created — it came from the air.

questions.stem: Why is the formula of water always H2O and never H3O in ordinary conditions?
options: A compound has a fixed ratio of atoms determined by how they bond
The ratio can actually vary freely
questions.explanation: Fixed composition is a defining property of compounds, and it follows from the bonding — unlike mixtures, whose proportions vary.

questions.stem: A student says burning is 'destroying' a substance. Give the better description.
options: The substance is destroyed and its atoms vanish
The substance reacts with oxygen to form new substances, and the atoms are conserved
questions.explanation: Nothing is destroyed at the atomic level. Burning is a chemical reaction, usually with oxygen, and the mass ends up in the products including gases.

questions.stem: Explain why the periodic table is described as a model rather than just a list.
options: Its arrangement predicts properties and relationships between elements
questions.explanation: Position carries meaning — elements in the same group behave similarly, which allowed properties of undiscovered elements to be predicted.

questions.stem: Two substances have the same elements but different properties. What is the most likely explanation?
options: One of them is not a real substance
One contains extra atoms of an element not listed
The atoms are joined in different ratios or arrangements
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide contain the same elements but differ in ratio, and behave completely differently.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for carbon?
questions.explanation: C is carbon, Ca is calcium and Co is cobalt. Capitalisation and letter count both matter.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for hydrogen?
questions.explanation: H is hydrogen, He is helium and Hg is mercury.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for nitrogen?
questions.explanation: N is nitrogen, Ni is nickel and Na is sodium.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for calcium?
questions.explanation: Ca is calcium; Cl is chlorine and C is carbon.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
questions.explanation: Potassium is K, from the Latin kalium. P is phosphorus.

questions.stem: What are the products of a reaction?
questions.explanation: Reactants go in and products come out.

questions.stem: What is combustion?
options: A substance reacting with oxygen, releasing energy
questions.explanation: Burning is combustion, a chemical reaction with oxygen.

questions.stem: What is rusting?
options: Iron reacting with oxygen and water to form iron oxide
questions.explanation: Rust is a new substance, so rusting is a chemical change.

questions.stem: How many different elements are in the compound NaCl?
questions.explanation: Sodium and chlorine — two elements bonded together.

questions.stem: How many oxygen atoms are in H2SO4?
questions.explanation: The subscript 4 after O gives four oxygen atoms.

questions.stem: What is the periodic table organised by?
options: The order in which elements were named
The relative abundance of each element on Earth
Properties and atomic structure of elements
The physical state of each element at room temperature
questions.explanation: Position reflects structure, which is why elements in the same group behave similarly.

questions.stem: Which is a mixture rather than a compound?
questions.explanation: Sea water contains several substances not chemically bonded, in varying proportions.

questions.stem: What is a reactant that is used up completely called?
questions.explanation: Once it runs out the reaction stops, however much of the other reactant remains.

questions.stem: What is the law of conservation of mass?
options: Mass is conserved only inside a sealed container
Total mass of reactants equals total mass of products
questions.explanation: Atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed.

questions.stem: Which of these describes a chemical change?
questions.explanation: Baking produces new substances that cannot be turned back.

questions.stem: Iron filings and sulfur are heated and form a new grey solid that is not magnetic. What happened?
options: A chemical reaction produced iron sulfide
questions.explanation: Loss of the iron's magnetism shows a new substance with different properties has formed.

questions.stem: Why does a burning candle in a sealed jar go out?
options: The oxygen available is used up
questions.explanation: Combustion needs oxygen, and a sealed jar has a limited supply.

questions.stem: Which pair of observations together most strongly indicate a chemical reaction?
options: The mixture dissolves and looks clear
A gas is produced and a colour change occurs that cannot be reversed
The mixture becomes warm and is stirred
The mixture changes shape and is poured
questions.explanation: Multiple signs together, especially irreversibility, are much stronger evidence than any single one.

questions.stem: A student heats copper in air and the mass increases. Explain.
options: Oxygen from the air has combined with the copper to form copper oxide
questions.explanation: Mass is conserved overall; the extra mass came from the air.

questions.stem: Why do chemical formulas use subscripts rather than ordinary numbers in front?
options: A subscript shows atoms within one molecule, while a number in front counts molecules
questions.explanation: 2H2O means two water molecules, each containing two hydrogens — the position of the number changes the meaning.

questions.stem: Which statement about elements and compounds is correct?
options: Elements always contain two types of atom
A compound can be broken into elements only by chemical means
An element can be broken into simpler substances chemically
Compounds and mixtures are the same
questions.explanation: Elements are already the simplest chemical substances.

questions.stem: Air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. Why is this a mixture?
options: The gases are not chemically bonded and the proportions can vary
Because it contains more than one gas, which always means a compound
questions.explanation: Variable proportions and no bonding are the defining features of a mixture.

questions.stem: Why is a chemical equation balanced?
options: To show that the same atoms are present before and after the reaction
questions.explanation: Balancing expresses conservation of mass at the atomic level.

questions.stem: Which change is physical despite appearing dramatic?
options: Dry ice producing clouds of vapour
questions.explanation: Sublimation of dry ice is a state change; the carbon dioxide is unchanged chemically.

questions.stem: A reaction produces bubbles that relight a glowing splint. Which gas is it?
questions.explanation: Relighting a glowing splint is the standard test for oxygen. Hydrogen gives a squeaky pop.

questions.stem: A gas turns limewater cloudy. Which gas is it?
questions.explanation: The limewater test is specific to carbon dioxide.

questions.stem: Why can a compound's properties not be predicted by averaging its elements' properties?
options: The properties are always the average
Chemical bonding produces an entirely new substance with its own properties
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride versus sodium and chlorine is the standard demonstration of this.

questions.stem: Why does a sealed flask show no mass change during a reaction that produces gas?
options: The gas remains inside the system, so nothing leaves
The gas condenses back into the mixture as it cools
The balance cannot detect a change that small
The gas pressure pushes up on the flask, offsetting the loss
questions.explanation: This is the classic demonstration of conservation of mass — the same reaction in an open flask appears to lose mass.

questions.stem: Which evidence would best distinguish a compound from a mixture of the same elements?
options: Measuring the total mass before and after heating to see whether material is lost
Observing whether the sample looks uniform to the eye and under a hand lens
Testing whether it conducts electricity once dissolved, as ionic substances do
Testing whether the components can be separated by physical means and whether the ratio is fixed
questions.explanation: Fixed ratio and resistance to physical separation are the defining features of a compound.

questions.stem: A student says burning magnesium 'creates light energy'. What is more accurate?
options: Chemical energy stored in the reactants is transformed into light and thermal energy
Energy is created in the reaction
questions.explanation: Energy is transformed, not created — the same conservation principle that applies to mass.

questions.stem: Two samples contain the same elements in different fixed ratios. What are they?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide are the standard example — same elements, different compounds.

questions.stem: Why does a powdered solid react faster than the same mass as a single lump?
options: Powder has far more surface area exposed to the other reactant
questions.explanation: Reaction happens at the surface, so increasing surface area increases the rate.

questions.stem: Which observation would most challenge the claim that a change was purely physical?
options: The original substance cannot be recovered by cooling, filtering or evaporating
questions.explanation: Irreversibility by physical means points to new substances having formed.

questions.stem: Why is the atomic theory described as a model?
options: Atoms are visible with a school microscope
Models are guesses with no evidence
It proposes unobservable particles whose behaviour explains observable evidence
questions.explanation: Its power is explanatory and predictive — it accounts for fixed ratios, conservation of mass and much more.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for chlorine?
questions.explanation: Cl is chlorine; C is carbon and Cr is chromium.

questions.stem: What is the chemical symbol for magnesium?
questions.explanation: Mg is magnesium; Mn is manganese.

questions.stem: How many atoms are in a molecule of NH3?
questions.explanation: One nitrogen plus three hydrogens gives four atoms.

questions.stem: What is a catalyst?
options: A substance that speeds up a reaction without being used up
questions.explanation: Catalysts lower the energy needed for a reaction to proceed.

questions.stem: Which is a sign of a chemical reaction in cooking?
questions.explanation: Browning creates new substances with new flavours and cannot be reversed.

questions.stem: What is oxidation in simple terms?
options: A reaction in which a substance loses oxygen
A reaction in which a substance combines with oxygen
A reaction that gives off light as it proceeds
A reaction that occurs only at high temperatures
questions.explanation: Rusting and burning are both oxidation reactions.

questions.stem: Which state symbol represents a gas in an equation?
questions.explanation: (s) is solid, (l) liquid and (aq) dissolved in water.

questions.stem: What does (aq) mean in a chemical equation?
questions.explanation: Aqueous means the substance is in water solution.

questions.stem: Which is an element made of two atoms joined together?
questions.explanation: O2 contains only oxygen atoms, so it is still an element despite being a molecule.

questions.stem: What happens to atoms during a chemical reaction?
options: They are rearranged into new combinations
questions.explanation: Chemical reactions rearrange atoms; changing one element into another requires nuclear processes.

questions.stem: Why does a reaction speed up when the temperature is raised?
options: Particles move faster and collide more often with more energy
Heat converts some reactant directly into product
questions.explanation: More frequent and more energetic collisions increase the rate.

questions.stem: A student mixes two solutions and the temperature drops. What does this indicate?
options: An endothermic change, taking energy from the surroundings
questions.explanation: Endothermic changes absorb energy; exothermic ones release it.

questions.stem: Which combination confirms a chemical change most convincingly?
options: The mixture is poured and changes shape
The mixture is cooled and thickens
A gas is produced, the mixture warms, and the product cannot be separated physically
The mixture is stirred and becomes uniform
questions.explanation: Several independent signs, especially irreversibility, together make a strong case.

questions.stem: Why do fireworks produce different colours?
options: Different metal compounds emit different colours when heated
Different amounts of gunpowder are used
questions.explanation: Metal salts give characteristic colours, which is also the basis of the flame test.

questions.stem: Why is the total mass unchanged when magnesium burns in a sealed container?
options: The oxygen that combines with it was already inside the container
questions.explanation: Sealing keeps the system closed, so conservation of mass is directly observable.

questions.stem: Why does milk souring count as a chemical change?
options: New substances with different taste and texture are formed irreversibly
questions.explanation: Bacteria produce lactic acid, which is a new substance.

questions.stem: Which statement about a compound's formula is correct?
options: It shows a fixed ratio determined by how the atoms bond
The ratio can be varied freely
It shows the mass of the compound
questions.explanation: Fixed composition is what distinguishes a compound from a mixture.

questions.stem: A reaction produces a gas and the open container loses 0.4 g. What can you conclude?
options: 0.4 g of gas escaped, and mass is conserved overall
questions.explanation: The lost mass is accounted for by the escaped gas, which could be captured to demonstrate this.

questions.stem: Why does powdered zinc react faster with acid than a zinc strip of the same mass?
options: Powder exposes far more surface area for collisions
The strip has more surface area
questions.explanation: Reaction occurs at the surface, and surface area rises sharply when a solid is divided.

questions.stem: Which is the strongest evidence that a colour change signals a reaction rather than dilution?
options: The new colour persists and the substance shows other new properties
questions.explanation: Dilution lightens colour but produces no new substance, so accompanying property changes are decisive.

questions.stem: Why is a word equation less informative than a chemical formula equation?
options: It does not show how many atoms of each element are involved
questions.explanation: Word equations name substances; formula equations show composition and can be balanced.
